newsitem.title: UK: Pearson up on talk of Lazard stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Pearson up on talk of Lazard stake sale.

text.p: Shares in Pearson Plc jumped in early trade on Monday on reports that the media and leisure company could sell its stakes in the Lazard investment banking group, dealers said.
By 0845 GMT Pearson shares were 13p higher at 761-1/2 after climbing as high as 766-3/4, their highest level since end-October.

"There was more talk in the Financial Times at the weekend about Pearson selling off its Lazard stake," one market-maker said. "It's not a new story but people are giving it more credence and it seems to be good for the shares."
Marjorie Scardino took over as chief executive of Pearson on January 8 and analysts have speculated that she could sell off Pearson's banking interests.
Equally Lazard was said to be looking to sell its stake in Pearson -- giving any bidder a potential platform to strike, though Lazard said it would not sell to a party that could be hostile.
French investment bank Lazard Freres told the Financial Times on Saturday that it might sell its holding of Pearson shares if Pearson sold its holding in the bank.
Lazard Freres senior partner Michel David-Weill said the bank would want to buy back the stake and would need to find the necessary funds.

The Financial Times, which is owned by Pearson, put the value of Lazard Freres' stake in Pearson at 360 million stg and said the linked Lazard investment banks in Paris, London and New York owned 48 million Pearson shares.
